Selling in a city this size

Las Vegas fills a basin on the floor of the Mojave Desert, ringed by mountains, at about 2,000 feet above sea level. The city covers roughly 142 square miles, and the urban area around it runs to about 540. A house in Centennial Hills and one near Downtown can share a Las Vegas address and still be very different properties.

The neighborhoods include Summerlin, Queensridge, The Lakes, Rancho, Lone Mountain, Peccole Ranch and Canyon Gate, each with its own mix of build years, lot sizes and homeowners associations. Those traits shape the repairs a buyer expects. Roofing, windows, air conditioning and wiring differ from one decade of construction to the next, and the gaps produce the repair lists that make a standard listing expensive.

Why owners sell fast here

Tourism, gaming and conventions run the local economy, and household income can rise and fall with visitor traffic and shift schedules. An owner who loses hours, moves for work or inherits a relative's house often has to sell on someone else's clock. Cash fits that, since the closing day is something you work out with the buyer and not something a lender dictates.

  • A new job or a move out of town.
  • An estate house with postponed maintenance and a stack of papers.
  • A landlord whose tenant is still in the unit and who wants a buyer willing to accept that.

Heat, floods and the inspection

Summers here are long and extremely hot, with July highs averaging 104.5 degrees Fahrenheit and only about 4.2 inches of rain a year. Air conditioning, roof membranes, stucco, irrigation lines and pool equipment all take a beating. Inspectors check how old the AC unit is before anything else, and a unit near the end of its life usually brings a request for a credit or replacement from a buyer with a loan. That is a major reason owners of older systems think about selling as-is.

Rain is rare but can arrive hard. Floods in the valley during the 1970s and early 1980s led to the creation of a regional flood control district in 1986. Homeowner's policies exclude flood damage, and the county directs owners to the National Flood Insurance Program. A lender that wants flood coverage on your parcel may raise it late in the process.

Disclosure form and transfer tax

Under NRS 113.130, anyone selling a home in Nevada completes the Real Estate Division's Form 547, the Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form, which lists known conditions that materially affect the property.

If the buyer closes without a completed form or without hearing about a known defect, treble damages are possible unless the buyer waived that right under NRS 113.150(6). Be honest and complete on every line.

Document or costRequirement
Seller disclosureForm 547, NRS 113.130
Base transfer tax$1.95 per $500 of value
Clark County add-on$0.60 per $500
Clark County total$2.55 per $500
Paperwork at recordingDeclaration of Value

A declaration of value has to ride along with each deed sent to the county recorder. NRS 375 lets the tax fall on either party, so put the payer in the contract.

Can a house stay a short-term rental after a sale?

Not automatically, since the city applies eligibility rules to each new license. Las Vegas treats a house or condominium rented to guests for fewer than 31 consecutive days as a short-term residential rental.

Under the city's 2026 instructions, a new license requires that the residence be at least 660 feet from any other short-term residential rental and 2,500 feet from a resort hotel, sit in a zone that allows the use, and have written HOA permission where an association exists. For a house that has been a rental, ask the Business Licensing Division how the license is treated at transfer, and give buyers a straight account.

Clark County property tax when you sell

Billing for Las Vegas property belongs to Clark County. A parcel with tax above $100 can be paid in installments on the third Monday of August and the first Mondays of October, January and March, while smaller bills are due in full in August. One bill a year goes out, and anyone without it by August 1 can ask for a copy on the automated phone system. NRS 361.483 sets late penalties beginning at 4 percent for a late installment.

Disagree with your value? The petition to the County Board of Equalization is due by January 15. Owner-occupants have another break under NRS 361.4723, which holds the yearly rise on a primary residence near 3 percent but excludes homes rented to others.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Las Vegas houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If you owe tax or an assessment

Owing property tax or a special assessment does not block a sale. Your title company requests a payoff, pays it from your proceeds and divides the installment now running between you and the buyer. A tax bill mailed once a year is easy to misplace, so look up the parcel with the Clark County Treasurer first and learn which installments are still open. Knowing the number before you speak with a buyer keeps the conversation short and lets the closing date be set without guessing. If the house was inherited, ask the Treasurer about every installment, because heirs sometimes find more than one unpaid.

What a cash sale looks like

When a buyer pays cash, no lender appraisal or underwriting slows things down. Typical steps run from an offer to a title search, the seller's disclosure, a signed contract, a closing at a title or escrow office and finally recording of the deed with its declaration of value.

How long yours takes depends on title, liens, tenants and how fast an HOA, if any, answers document requests. Cash Home Buyers names no price in advance. We view the house as it stands, and declining an offer costs nothing.

What Las Vegas sellers usually face

These situations often make a conventional listing hard.

  • An old AC system, roof or pool that would draw repair requests.
  • A house from an estate that needs probate, or a transfer on death deed, completed first.
  • A tenant living there, or a rental with a short-term license in question.
  • HOA paperwork, assessments or violations to resolve before closing.
  • A loan balance, tax installment or other lien to pay off at the table.

A cash sale can handle each one, although the order of the work changes. Assemble the deed, newest tax bill, HOA statements and mortgage payoff before you call a buyer to save time.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What transfer tax comes with a Las Vegas house sale?

Clark County charges $2.55 per $500 of value, which combines the state's $1.95 with a $0.60 county add-on. The contract names the payer, since NRS 375 allows either side.

Is a seller disclosure required in Nevada?

Yes, NRS 113.130 requires it of residential sellers. Skipping it, or hiding a known defect, can expose you to treble damages unless the buyer waived that right.

When are Clark County property taxes due?

Third Monday in August. Above $100, a parcel may be split into four installments, the later ones landing on the first Mondays of October, January and March.

What is the deadline to appeal a Las Vegas assessment?

January 15 is the cutoff for petitioning the Clark County Board of Equalization, and a weekend or holiday shifts it to the next business day.

Does the turf removal law force me to tear out my grass before selling?

Not if it is a single-family home. The water authority says the law, which bars Colorado River water on nonfunctional grass from 2027, targets commercial, multi-family, government and other properties and leaves single-family yards out.

Henderson in brief

Henderson is a Clark County city about 16 miles southeast of Las Vegas, at roughly 1,867 feet of elevation and covering about 107 square miles. The July 1, 2025 population estimate is 353,289, second in Nevada behind Las Vegas. A Henderson seller shares a market, an airport and a school district with the bigger neighbor but deals with a different city hall.

Henderson incorporated on April 16, 1953. Most of its later growth took the form of master-planned communities: Green Valley first, then Anthem, Lake Las Vegas and Seven Hills. Many have homeowners associations, which is worth confirming for your own address before you list.

  • Green Valley, the first large master-planned neighborhood.
  • Anthem, Seven Hills and Lake Las Vegas, later communities with their own rules.
  • Older parts of the city, where you should check whether any association applies.

Heat, flash floods and repairs

Summer heat is hardest on roofs, cooling equipment, paint and landscaping. If the air conditioner is old or the roof leaks, a buyer with a mortgage will likely ask for repairs, whereas a cash buyer may take the house unrepaired and lower the offer accordingly.

Valley storms can bring flash flooding. Homeowner's insurance leaves flood damage out, and the county directs owners to the National Flood Insurance Program. A regional flood control district created in 1986 handles drainage across the valley. Find out from your insurance agent if your parcel sits in a mapped flood zone, so you hear it before a buyer's lender does.

Short-term rentals

Henderson allows short-term vacation rentals only with annual city registration, and some developments are on a prohibited list where the city will not register a property. The city lists a non-refundable registration fee of $848, a certification class for the owner and the local contact, a Nevada business license in the owner's name, and a registered local contact who is either certified or a property manager under NRS 645. Registered properties must also file the room tax report and pay transient lodging tax monthly.

When the home sits in a common-interest community, the city's acknowledgement form requires that the rental be expressly authorized by the association.

A house that has hosted visitors should come with a clear statement of whether its registration is current. Do not assume the registration passes to a new owner without asking the city.

Turf law and your HOA

A 2021 Nevada law on nonfunctional turf leaves grass in single-family yards alone. Starting in 2027 it bars Colorado River water from member agencies on nonfunctional grass, and the water authority says it reaches commercial, multi-family, government and other properties.

Living in a condominium, or in an association with shared lawns? Then the deadline lands on the association, and a special assessment could show up in its budget. Buyers will ask. Get the association's most recent statement before listing.

Disclosures and transfer tax

NRS 113.130 requires Henderson sellers to complete Nevada's Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form. A buyer who closes with no completed form, or with no word of a known defect, can claim treble damages unless that right was waived.

The Clark County rate runs $2.55 per $500 of value: $1.95 from the state and $0.60 from the county. A declaration of value goes to the county recorder with the deed. NRS 375 lets either side be charged, so look at your contract to see who pays.

StepWho handles it
Seller disclosure, Form 547Seller

Property tax billing and appeals

Henderson parcels are billed by Clark County. The full amount falls due the third Monday in August, or in installments for parcels over $100, with later ones on the first Mondays of October, January and March. NRS 361.483 puts a 4 percent penalty on a late installment and raises it as more are missed.

Anyone disputing an assessed value has until January 15 of the fiscal year to petition the County Board of Equalization, with a weekend or holiday pushing the date to the next business day.

NRS 361.4723 holds a primary residence to about a 3 percent annual rise in its tax bill. Because the statute treats a home rented to anyone beyond the owner and family as something else, a former rental may miss out.

If you owe tax or HOA dues

Both open tax and unpaid association dues can be paid off at closing. Get a payoff from the Clark County Treasurer and a current statement from the association, pass both to the title company and let your proceeds cover them. A mortgage or recorded lien works the same way.

Association paperwork can drag, so ask early. Buyers like to read the governing documents and a list of assessments before committing.

From offer to closing in Henderson

The order of events is simple. A buyer reviews the house and makes an offer, a title search confirms ownership and flags liens, and you sign the contract together with the disclosure. Closing takes place at a title or escrow office, and the deed and declaration of value then go to the Clark County Recorder.

The items that most often add time in a Henderson sale are association paperwork, a short-term rental registration that needs sorting out, and an estate that has not finished probate. Raise whichever applies on your first call, and the buyer can plan around it.

Preparing a Henderson house for a quick sale

Speed comes from preparation. Before anyone makes an offer, find your deed, the most recent tax bill and any mortgage statement. If the house has an association, order the dues statement and the governing documents at the same time, because those requests move at the association's pace and not yours. Write down what you know about the roof, the cooling system, plumbing and any past water damage. If the house was ever rented to visitors, locate the registration paperwork too.

With that folder in hand, the title company can order its search at once, and a buyer sees a seller who is organized. Sellers who skip this step usually lose days to document requests, not to the buyer.

How a cash sale works in Henderson

A cash buyer brings no mortgage, which removes the wait for a lender appraisal. Your side is unchanged: hand over the disclosure, deliver clear title, square up any HOA balance, pay a mortgage or lien at closing and sign the deed.

Cash Home Buyers looks at the house in its current state and quotes no number beforehand. An offer you decide against costs you nothing.

  • Gather the deed, a loan payoff statement and your newest tax bill.
  • Ask for an up-to-date HOA statement and governing documents.
  • Note known repairs so the disclosure is complete.

Frequently asked questions

How far is Henderson from Las Vegas?

Roughly 16 miles to the southeast. Both cities sit in Clark County and share a school district.

How much does a Henderson short-term rental registration cost?

$848 per property each year, and it cannot be refunded. On top of that, owners need a Nevada business license, a certification class and a qualifying local contact.

Is there a transfer tax when I sell in Henderson?

Yes, $2.55 per $500 of value in Clark County. Either side can be charged under NRS 375, so your contract settles who pays.

Do I need to remove my front lawn before selling?

No. The water authority confirms that the turf law leaves single-family grass, front and back, alone.

When can I appeal my Henderson property tax assessment?

By January 15, with the County Board of Equalization. A weekend or holiday on that date moves the deadline to the next business day.

Selling in North Las Vegas?

About North Las Vegas

North Las Vegas sits northeast of Las Vegas in Clark County, out in the Mojave Desert. The 2020 census counted 262,527 people, which puts it fourth among Nevada cities. Streets near the original townsite (locals say Old Town) hold older lots, while Aliante and Eldorado are newer planned communities with recent construction.

Condition is all over the map here. Our offers reflect what the house is today, so no one hands you a lender's punch list.

Desert heat and what it wears out

Summer is the hard season here. July afternoons average roughly 105 degrees, and rain totals only about 4.6 inches a year. Winter nights can dip below freezing, and monsoon storms sometimes dump heavy rain in summer.

Inspectors and buyers usually start with:

  • The air conditioner, since it works nearly year-round and its age shows
  • Roof tile or membrane that has baked in the sun for years
  • Block walls and fences, because damaged ones can draw a city code complaint

Nothing on that list has to be repaired before a cash closing. Problems you are already aware of go on the disclosure form regardless.

Code enforcement and short-term rental rules

Two city rules trip up sellers most: open code cases and short-term rental permits. The city administers both, and the county does not.

The Code Enforcement Division goes after:

  • Vacant buildings that are not boarded or secured
  • Junk, litter, garbage and tall weeds
  • Junk vehicles and signs posted where they are not allowed
  • Illegal home businesses
  • Obstructed streets or sidewalks, and damaged fences or block walls

Staff begin with notices and education. If an owner ignores them, the division can abate the nuisance itself or issue criminal citations. Owners can request an appeal hearing. Settle an open case before closing, or tell the buyer in writing that it exists.

Short-term rentals are harder. Ordinance 3127 took effect in June 2022 and calls for a Conditional Use Permit ahead of any business license. Applicants bring a notarized letter from the HOA, and the site must sit 660 feet from other short-term rentals and 2,500 feet from resort hotels. Planning and Zoning answers questions at (702) 633-1537.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your North Las Vegas house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Seller disclosure under Nevada law

Nevada makes the owner complete a written condition form no later than 10 days before the property changes hands. Paying cash changes nothing here. NRS 113.130 puts the task on the seller personally; the seller or the listing agent then delivers it to the buyer or the buyer's agent. If something new turns up, or a disclosed problem gets worse, you owe the buyer a written update before closing.

A handful of transfers are exempt, among them foreclosure sales, transfers among co-owners, spouses or close relatives, the first sale of a new house by the contractor who built it, and some sales by a personal representative or trustee. Buyers cannot waive the form.

Transfer tax and HOA documents

The Clark County transfer tax rate is $2.55 for every $500 of value, made up of the state's $1.95 and a $0.60 county add-on. It is collected by the County Recorder at the time the deed is recorded. Both sides are liable together and individually under state rules, which is why the sales contract should name who pays it. NRS 375.090 exempts certain transfers, such as one between former spouses under a divorce decree or a deed that becomes effective at death.

For a home in an HOA, NRS 116.4109 requires a resale package covering the governing documents, any unpaid assessments and fines, and the budget. After the buyer gets it, a five-calendar-day cancellation window runs to midnight.

Property tax due dates and penalties

The Clark County Treasurer sends one real property tax bill a year. When it is over $100, you may split it into four payments, though the spacing is uneven rather than quarterly.

Clark County installment schedule
InstallmentDue date
FirstThird Monday in August
SecondFirst Monday in October
ThirdFirst Monday in January
FourthFirst Monday in March

Payments need to land within 10 days of each due date. One late installment draws a 4 percent penalty. Accounts still unpaid at the end of April are advertised as delinquent, and if money is owed on the first Monday in June the county holds the parcel under a two-year redemption period that accrues 10 percent interest yearly.

Behind on taxes? Request a payoff amount from the Treasurer well before closing. The office is at 500 S Grand Central Pkwy, (702) 455-4323, open Monday through Thursday.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy North Las Vegas houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Unpaid tax will not stop a cash purchase. Title work turns up the balance, and escrow subtracts it from what you receive, just like a loan payoff. Ask the Treasurer for a written number early so you can weigh any offer against your likely take-home.

Before phoning, pull together the parcel number, your latest bill and any letter from the city or HOA. Having that on hand shortens escrow.

What a cash sale looks like step by step

No underwriting queue means the schedule is set by title work and signatures. You still handle the Nevada items: the disclosure, the recorded deed, transfer tax and any HOA documents.

  1. Give us the address and a plain-language description; a written offer comes back.
  2. A title company opens escrow and runs a search for liens, back taxes and judgments.
  3. You complete the seller's disclosure and gather any HOA package.
  4. You sign the deed, which is recorded by the Clark County Recorder with a Declaration of Value.
  5. Escrow settles liens and fees, then sends you what is left.

We buy North Las Vegas houses as-is. Mention tenants, liens or half-done repairs at the outset and the number we give you already accounts for them. Declining costs you nothing.

Closing timing is mostly up to you. Because no loan has to be approved, many owners pick a date around a move, a job change or a probate hearing. The title company confirms the deed is clean, the Recorder logs it, and funds are released from escrow once the deed is on record. If an HOA is involved, order the resale package right away, since the buyer's cancellation window starts only when it is delivered and it can hold things up if it comes late.

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to disclose problems if I sell my North Las Vegas house for cash?

Yes, and a cash deal gets no break. The form must be delivered at least 10 days ahead of conveyance. You list what you know of, nothing more, but anything new discovered before closing goes to the buyer in writing.

How much is the transfer tax on a North Las Vegas sale?

The county rate is $2.55 on each $500 of value: $1.95 for the state and $0.60 for Clark County. Collection happens at recording, and the contract decides who bears it.

Can a North Las Vegas buyer turn my house into a short-term rental?

Not without a Conditional Use Permit, which must be in hand before a business license is requested. Distance limits apply too, and an HOA letter is required where there is an association.

What happens if code enforcement has an open case on my house?

The city can abate the nuisance or cite you when notices are ignored, and you may appeal. Try to close the case before the sale, and disclose any that remain open.

When are Clark County property taxes due?

Mid-to-late August, on the third Monday. Bills above $100 can be split across that date plus the first Mondays of October, January and March, and a late installment costs 4 percent.

Reno at a glance

Reno is the seat of Washoe County, tucked against the California line in the Truckee River valley below the Sierra Nevada. Elevation is around 4,400 feet, and Lake Tahoe lies about 23 miles to the southwest. The 2020 census counted 264,165 residents. The University of Nevada, Reno and the casino and tourism trade shape much of the housing market, and Reno shares the Truckee Meadows valley with Sparks.

Houses here run from older central neighborhoods to hillside and western-edge homes, so condition, exposure and lot all affect what a buyer will offer.

Winter, wind and what they do to a house

Reno has cold, dry winters and hot summers, so a single year can bring a deep freeze, high wind and long stretches of heat. Temperatures hit freezing or lower on 122 days a year, while about 65 days reach 90 degrees or more. The record low is minus 17 degrees and the record high 108. Most moisture falls in fall, winter and spring, and the western side of town gets three to four times what the east side does.

Wear shows up in predictable places:

  • Pipes, hose bibs and exterior paint, after repeated freeze and thaw
  • Roofing and fencing, battered by wind and big temperature swings
  • Western-edge properties, which see far more precipitation than eastern ones

Deferred maintenance on any of this is not something you must fix before a cash sale. Defects you know about belong on the Nevada disclosure form.

How much wildfire and earthquake risk does Reno have?

Wildfire is the largest natural hazard for Reno homes, especially on the southwest side, and most homes in the area carry some risk. A few events show how real that is:

EventWhat happened
November 2011 Caughlin firePowerline arcing started a fire in southwest Reno that destroyed 26 homes
January 2012 Washoe Drive fireFireplace ashes started a fire that destroyed 29 homes, with about 10,000 people evacuated
September 2024 Davis FireForested areas of southwest Reno burned, 14 structures were lost and about 20,000 people were evacuated
February 2008 earthquake swarmThe largest quake was about magnitude 4.9, centered near Somersett, Mogul and Verdi, and many homes were damaged

If your house backs onto a forested edge, say so on the disclosure form, along with any smoke or fire damage.

Code enforcement and liens

Reno's Code Enforcement department handles property maintenance, and an open violation can end up recorded against your title. The municipal code covers inoperable vehicles, trash and debris, overgrown landscaping, work without permits and zoning violations. The usual sequence runs like this:

  1. A warning of violation letter sets a compliance date, generally about 30 days out.
  2. If the problem remains, an administrative citation follows: $100 the first time, $250 the second and $500 the third on residential property.
  3. A notice of intent to record can lead to a notice of violation lien filed with the Washoe County Recorder.
  4. The lien comes off only after the work is fixed and all fines and fees are paid.

Owners can appeal through the City Clerk's office, and code officers have no authority to waive or reduce fines. Questions and complaints go to Reno Direct at 775-334-4636.

Some common problems sellers overlook: vehicles cannot be parked in the front yard, inoperable ones must be screened, and couches, mattresses and appliances cannot sit in view in a front or side yard. Tidy these up before photos or a walkthrough, and find out whether a lien has already been recorded. The city's 2024 building codes took effect July 1, 2025, so if you are finishing unpermitted work before a sale, check permit status with Building first.

What does Nevada require from a Reno seller?

A Reno seller completes the state disclosure form at least 10 days before conveyance, and cash deals are not exempt. Under NRS 113.130 the owner, not the agent, fills it out, and the buyer cannot waive it. The exceptions cover foreclosure sales, transfers between spouses or close relatives and some trustee or personal representative sales.
